recipes.name: Spicy stir-fried pork (Dwaejigogi-bokkeum)
ingredients: 1 pound pork belly, cut into bite-sized pieces (1/8 inch thick)
instructions: Heat up a large, thick skillet (or pan) over medium high heat.
Add pork, hot pepper paste, soy sauce, sugar, hot pepper flakes, black pepper, and toasted sesame oil.
Mix it well, stirring with a wooden spoon. Cook it for a few minutes until the pork is well mixed with the seasonings.
Add garlic, ginger, onion, and green onions. Stir and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the pork is fully cooked and juicy and a little crispy.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with rice, kimchi, lettuce, ssamjang, and more side dishes.

instruction_sections.text: Cook over medium-high heat so the pork stir-fries nicely without becoming watery. If the heat is too low, the ingredients release liquid and the dish becomes watery. Stir as you cook to keep the pork and seasonings from burning.

I recommend making just enough to enjoy right away. If you have leftovers, refrigerate them and eat them by the next day. You can reheat them in the microwave, or put them in a skillet with a little water and stir-fry over medium-high heat until the pork is tender and heated through.
